title: Agility Robotics and Churchill Capital Corp XI S-4 Registration Statement Declared Effective by SEC in Connection with Proposed Business Combination
source: Business Wire (Agility Robotics and Churchill Capital Corp XI release, carried by FinancialContent)
machine_does: Agility Robotics, maker of the Digit humanoid (earlier generations logged 65,000+ real-world hours; customers named: Schaeffler, GXO, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada), announced the SEC declared its merger filing with Churchill Capital Corp XI effective on 13 Oct; Churchill XI shareholders vote on 2 Nov 2026 and the company would trade as AGLT on Nasdaq.
why_it_matters: If the 2 Nov vote passes, Agility becomes, by the company's own description, the only US publicly listed pure-play humanoid robot company, a first public-market price for a humanoid maker.
date_checked: Business Wire release text read: 'declared effective by the SEC on October 13, 2026', page stamp 2026-10-13T20:32:00Z (inside the window). Same-day coverage by Unite.AI 21:12Z, Reuters wire via TradingView, Investing.com, StreetInsider. No Agility item in the 10-10, 10-11, 10-12 pools. Raise size (over $620M) and $2.5B figure appear only in Securities.io and FourWeekMBA headlines, not verified.

title: Robot seized by German police after allegedly groping teenage girl
machine_does: A red-and-gold robot, 120 cm tall (widely reported as a humanoid), allegedly approached a 16-year-old girl from behind near a fast-food outlet in Cologne close to midnight on Saturday 10 Oct, grabbed her buttocks and made thrusting motions. Police seized it and two phones, and are investigating its 16-year-old owner and a 19-year-old companion, who allegedly streamed it live, to establish whether they were controlling the robot.
why_it_matters: A test case for who is responsible when a remotely operated robot harms someone: the operator, the owner or the maker; it also hands critics of home humanoids a vivid example.
date_checked: BBC page stamp 2026-10-13T23:50:23Z. CAUTION, older event: Cologne police statement 261012-2-K and first reports (STERN.de 12 Oct 14:14Z, Daily Mail, CTV, NY Post 12 Oct 14:59-18:40Z) came BEFORE the window opens; included because the main wave (BBC, Times, Telegraph, Independent, Mashable, SCMP, Economic Times, Times of India, WION, Zee, News18, Firstpost, Japan Today, and more, 25+ outlets by my count) ran inside the window and BBC/AP carry the new probe of two teens. title: China's Astribot Raises Fourth Round in Six Months, Valuation Jumps to 15 Billion Yuan
machine_does: Astribot, a Chinese maker of general-purpose humanoid robots (S and T series, combined capacity at the 10,000-unit level, own Lumo foundation model; customers named: Golden Horse, ThunderSoft, JD.com), announced on 13 Oct a new round of 1 billion yuan (about $149M) at a 15 billion yuan (about $2.2B) valuation, led by Toukong Donghai (Shenzhen Investment Holdings); its fourth round in about six months.
why_it_matters: Humanoid funding in China is arriving every few weeks and valuations are rising fast: the valuation passed 10 billion yuan only in June.
date_checked: Article text says 'announced on October 13'; page stamp 2026-10-13T07:26:04Z (inside the window). title: Korea Clears Safety Rules to Put 20 Humanoid Robots on Factory Floors
machine_does: South Korea's trade ministry granted Robros a regulatory exemption to run 20 bipedal humanoids beside human workers on real production lines: cleaning semiconductor packaging parts at Nepes, placing car body parts at Sungwoo Hitech, stacking ship scaffolding brackets at HD Hyundai Samho and moving refrigerated packaging at Delivery Lab; the test data will be used to rewrite safety standards.
why_it_matters: It is the first time Korea lets humanoids work on live factory floors under rewritten safety rules, a model other governments may copy.
date_checked: Ministry's 6th Industrial Convergence Regulatory Sandbox Review Committee met on 13 Oct (KST). Updated page stamp 2026.10.14 07:40:40 KST = 2026-10-13T22:40:40Z (inside the window). Its first version ran at 2026-10-13T06:00:05Z, 32 minutes before the window opened; BigGo Finance also carried it at 10:55Z. Not in the 10-10..10-12 pools.

title: Shanghai Targets 8,000 Humanoid Robots in Factories by 2028
source: Seoul Economic Daily (citing Chinese media including The Paper)
machine_does: Shanghai launched an action plan (four projects, 19 core tasks) at the opening of the 26th China International Industry Fair that sets a goal of putting 8,000 humanoid robots to work in factories by 2028.
why_it_matters: A city sets a hard number for humanoids on factory floors, a gauge of how fast China intends to scale the machines.
date_checked: Page stamp 2026.10.14 06:20:07 KST = 2026-10-13T21:20:07Z; article says Chinese media reported the plan on the 13th, at the fair opening. Inside the window. The 12 Oct pool carried a different CIIF item (JAKA wheeled humanoid), not this plan.

title: 'Human vs. Robot' cage match was a hit. State says event was illegal, but organizers aren't concerned
machine_does: Three remotely operated humanoid robots fought influencer Frankie LaPenna in MMA-style fights in a cage in San Francisco on 18 Sept, staged by REK (Robot Entertainment Kombat); he beat two of the three and the videos drew 10 million+ YouTube views. California's State Athletic Commission says the event needed its approval and has issued a cease-and-desist order; organizers argue the law covers contests between people, not robots.
why_it_matters: The first regulator ruling on robot combat entertainment, and a sign of how humanoids are being used for spectacle before they are used for work.
date_checked: LA Times page stamp 2026-10-13T18:52:53Z (11:52 AM PT). Event itself was 18 Sept; the new development inside the window is the commission's cease-and-desist and the LA Times report. Possibly related to the 12 Oct pool item C11-17 ('I watched 6-foot robots fight with blades. This is San Francisco now'), which is a different, earlier piece.

title: Gemini 4 Argon for Robotics
machine_does: Google's new Gemini 4 Argon model, as shown in Google's own demos, controlled a Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped to step on a foot-pedal bin and throw away soda cans after practising in a simulated copy, and steered a robot arm to stand a fallen mug upright and put a napkin in it; Google reports 87% on the ERQA embodied-reasoning benchmark, which it says beats every other frontier model.
why_it_matters: Google's flagship model launched on 13 Oct with robot control as a headline use, so the model race now includes physical robots.
date_checked: Post dated OCT. 13, 2026 (author Kanishka Rao); blog.google RSS stamp 2026-10-13T16:02:42Z. CNET, Business Insider, Times of India, Financial Express and 36Kr (14 Oct) covered the Argon launch the same day. The 87% and 'beats every frontier model' are Google's own claims. The 11 Oct pool had only a Gemini 4 Carbon rumour, not this launch.

title: Physical Intelligence Opens Pi API Beta for Robot Foundation Models
machine_does: Physical Intelligence, maker of the pi0 and pi0.5 general robot models, opened a waitlist beta of its Pi API on 13 Oct: outside developers upload robot data, fine-tune the latest model on hosted compute and run it on their own robot.
why_it_matters: Robot makers can rent a ready-made general robot brain instead of building one, which could speed up how many robots do useful work.
date_checked: Unite.AI page says 'announced the Pi API beta on October 13, 2026'; RSS stamp 2026-10-13T23:09:21Z. NOTE: the Unite.AI piece is bylined to an AI research agent; the primary source is Physical Intelligence's own announcement, which I did not fetch. No Physical Intelligence API item in the 10-10..10-12 pools (Ultra's tie-up with Physical Intelligence on 10 Oct is a different story).

title: US Army to stand up command for unmanned and autonomous warfare
machine_does: An Oct. 1 memo signed by Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle orders the U.S. Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command (FASCOM) to be set up and puts one office in charge of buying the Army's priority autonomous systems, reported a day after Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new four-star command for unmanned and autonomous warfare.
why_it_matters: The largest US military branch is reorganising around drones and autonomous machines, a shift other armies will watch and copy.
date_checked: Military Times byline Michael Scanlon, Oct 13, 2026 04:15 PM, meta 2026-10-13T16:15:00Z (inside the window). Follow-ups: Federal News Network 14 Oct 05:16Z, SOFX 04:49Z, AL.com 13 Oct 20:49Z (Alabama base chosen). OVERLAP: the 11 Oct pool has C13-13 'Hegseth says 20% of senior military officers will be cut, unveils new AI command'; the Army FASCOM memo is a separate, newer step, but the editors should link the two.

title: Google DeepMind to Open Robotics Lab in Boston Area
source: AI Insider (citing Aaron Saunders' LinkedIn post)
machine_does: Google DeepMind is building a new robotics hardware lab in Cambridge, Massachusetts, to bring advanced AI into physical machines; Aaron Saunders, former Boston Dynamics chief technology officer and now DeepMind vice president of embodied systems and robotics, announced it on LinkedIn on Monday 12 Oct while recruiting machinists, engineers and researchers.
why_it_matters: Google is putting its own robot hardware lab beside Boston Dynamics' home turf, run by that company's former technology chief.

title: NEURA Robotics Introduces Neuron AI: The Brain of the Physical World
machine_does: NEURA Robotics of Metzingen, Germany, introduced Neuron AI, a foundation model that combines 3D vision, touch, audio, robot state and language with memory, so a robot can act on information a camera alone misses and keep context when an object leaves its view.
why_it_matters: Another robot maker is selling a touch-and-vision brain for robots, and a European one at that, as the physical-AI model race widens.
date_checked: Release dateline 'Oct 14, 2026'; Business Wire RSS stamp 2026-10-14T06:29:00Z, Eagle-Tribune copy 06:30:23Z, so only about 3 minutes inside the window end. I could not render the Business Wire page itself (text read from the Eagle-Tribune copy). Company claims only; no independent test.

title: Avatar comes to life: Honda's new robot mirrors human movements to work remotely
machine_does: At CEATEC 2026 in Japan on 13 Oct, Honda demonstrated its Avatar Robot, a remotely operated robotic hand with 16 actuated joints, up to 50 newtons of fingertip force and 288 tactile-sensor channels, so a person can do physical work far away (maintenance, medical support, disaster response, space); Honda says it passed 450,000 durability cycles.
why_it_matters: A major carmaker is showing a remote-work robot hand aimed at jobs too dangerous or too distant for people.
date_checked: Interesting Engineering stamp 2026-10-13T22:04:35Z; the article embeds Honda Japan's post dated October 13, 2026 from CEATEC 2026. Inside the window. Specs are Honda's own figures as relayed by the outlet. Not in the 10-10..10-12 pools.
